target_customer: Consumers who want a screenless, privacy focused voice AI device
problem: Phones and earlier AI wearables are slow, always listening or awkward for quick voice questions. Button aims for a press to talk device that answers in about half a second.
business_model: Hardware sale ($179 listed, $229 regular) plus optional Button AI Pro subscription at $7.99 per month, or bring your own API key

founders.name: Chris Nolet
prior_employers: Apple, staff software engineer on Vision Pro
previous_startups: Earlier startup, not named in sources (second-time founder)
founders.background_notes: YC page says mechanical engineering background and former venture partner. Education not stated.

founders.name: Ryan Burgoyne
founders.background_notes: YC launch post names a co-founder Ryan; the surname and CTO title come from a StartupHub article only.

competitors.name: AI pendants and pins (Friend, Plaud, Limitless, Bee)
competitors.what: Wearable AI devices for notes, assistance and companionship; Limitless was acquired by Meta and Bee by Amazon
competitors.traction_then: Category had a comeback at CES 2026 after the failure of Humane's AI Pin, whose servers were shut down in early 2025

technical_complexity.rationale: Custom hardware with low latency voice pipeline, Bluetooth link to the phone, a speaker and manufacturing. Hardware plus real time AI is hard for a two person team, though the founders shipped Vision Pro hardware at Apple.

defensibility.rationale: Speed and privacy are product choices that rivals can copy, and phones, Apple and OpenAI hardware are expected to compete. The founders' device engineering experience is the main edge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Apple is reportedly developing an AI pin and OpenAI is working on hardware per a Jan 2026 article; Meta and Amazon bought wearable startups in 2025. No direct copy of Button found.

market_need_then: Early AI wearables such as Humane's pin failed, but pendants returned at CES 2026. Button's preorders and launch press exist, but sales volume is unknown.

branding.domain_note: buttoncomputer.com, with the word Computer added to the brand

identity.visual_style: Device described as roughly iPod Shuffle sized and clip-on
identity.voice_and_tone: Privacy first, ambitious: 'building the conversational computer from sci-fi'

branding.brand_signature: A single physical button as the whole interface
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by Notebookcheck, Uncrate and smaller outlets; the company site claims TechCrunch and Wired features that were not found in search

brand_strength.rationale: The name literally describes the interaction and the product is easy to explain, with international launch press. The word button is generic for search, and no community was found.

outcome_analysis: Preorder stage with first US shipments listed for 15 December 2026, so there is no outcome yet. Strengths are founders who worked on Vision Pro hardware and a simple privacy story. The main risks are hardware execution, the poor record of earlier AI wearables, and big platforms entering the category.
notes: No funding found. YC page lists team size 1 while the launch post names two founders. The site shows conflicting stock text and two shipping descriptions (15 Dec 2026 or end of 2026). The Wired and TechCrunch claims on the site were not confirmed. Competitor list is a category entry because named rivals share one dated source.
